_comment: Ordered provider lanes, and within each an ordered model fallback list.
Model names live here and NEVER in code: free catalogues churn, and providers have been
observed silently deleting free models. A 404 falls through to the next entry and logs loudly.
rpm sits deliberately under the published ceiling. rpd is the SUM of the per-model daily
allowances in the list below, because the router walks every model and each one meters
separately - Gemini 500+20+20+20, Groq 1000 x 3. Both numbers were fiction until 8 August 2026
(13/1000 and 28/14400, invented); they are now read off each provider's own dashboard, and the
quota readout in Diagnostics is only as honest as they are.
ORDER WITHIN A LANE IS THE QUOTA POLICY, and it is not the same as quality order. Gemini's free
tier gives gemini-3.1-flash-lite 500 requests a day and 15 a minute, while the flash models get
TWENTY a day each. Leading with a flash model spent a whole evening's allowance in one sitting
and left 498 requests untouched on the model nobody reached. The big allowance leads; the
others sit behind it as genuine fallbacks.
gemini-2.5-flash-lite is absent on purpose: a live key returned 404 'no longer available' for
it while 2.5-flash on the same key answered 429, so it is dead rather than merely busy. Keeping
a guaranteed 404 in the walk buys nothing and costs a round trip.
LANE ORDER IS THE COST POLICY. The router walks this list top to bottom, so the free lanes are
tried first and the paid ones only answer what the free tiers could not. Move a paid lane up
if you would rather have its quality on every line and are willing to pay for it.
A lane with no key entered is skipped in silence, so shipping openai and anthropic enabled
costs nothing until someone deliberately pastes a key into Settings.
2026-08: the entire Gemini 2.x list died and this is what that churn actually looks like.
gemini-2.0-flash was shut down on 1 June 2026 - a guaranteed 404 that had been sitting in this
file as the middle fallback. gemini-2.5-flash and -flash-lite both began returning 404 'no
longer available' to NEWLY CREATED keys around 9 July, while Google's own deprecation page
still lists them as active with no shutdown date. So the same file worked on an older key and
failed completely on a new one, which is exactly how it was found. Their real shutdown is
16 October 2026.
gemini-2.5-flash stays LAST because keys created before July can still use it, and it costs
nothing to try after the others. gemini-2.5-flash-lite is dropped rather than kept beside it:
one tail entry for a dying family is a fallback, two is noise in the log.
2026-08, and within hours of the Gemini fix: Groq's list had died too, which is how the app
came to show 'translation failed' with two keys that both passed the key test. Groq deprecated
qwen/qwen3-32b and llama-3.3-70b-versatile on 17 June 2026 and stopped serving them during
August. Both free lanes were therefore empty at the same time, and the app's only symptom was
the English fallback - the router did exactly what it promises and there was simply nothing
left to route to. Replaced with the two production models Groq itself names as the migration
target. qwen/qwen3.6-27b is deliberately NOT included: it is preview-tier, and preview is what
churns. Their Arabic has not been compared against the old llama model - nobody has measured
it, so if the Arabic reads worse after this change, that is the reason and it is worth saying
out loud rather than assuming the lane is simply 'working' again.
The lesson from having this happen twice in one day: a lane whose every model is gone is not a
rare event, it is the normal end of a free model's life, and it arrives without warning. Check
both lanes against each provider's own /models endpoint before blaming anything else.
maxOutputTokens is a PER-MODEL number now, and on Groq it is the single most important number
in this file. A models[] entry may be a plain string or an object carrying overrides; both
forms are read forever, because the string form is what every models.json already installed
contains.
Why it moved. 'Tokens cost nothing that matters here, the workload is request-limited' was
true of Gemini and false of Groq, and nobody checked. Groq admits a request against
prompt_tokens + max_tokens - what you RESERVE, not what the answer costs - against a per-minute
token ceiling of 8,000 for the gpt-oss models and 12,000 for llama. At maxOutputTokens 4096
every line reserved 4,203 of 8,000, so the SECOND line inside any minute was refused; all three
models then refused in turn, the router put the whole lane in a sixty-second cooldown, and the
log said 'groq in cooldown, skipping' on every line after that. Groq was never slow - measured
8 August 2026 it answers in 0.09-0.74s - and it was never refusing on principle. We were
withholding half its per-minute allowance from ourselves on every single line.
reasoningEffort is the other half. gpt-oss-120b at default effort spends ~360 tokens thinking
about a one-line subtitle; at 'low' it spends 5 and the Arabic is no worse. That is what makes
a small maxOutputTokens safe rather than a repeat of the v0.5.0 disaster, where a 300-token
budget was consumed entirely by reasoning and EVERY completion came back empty while the key
test passed. The two numbers have to move together, which is exactly why they belong on the
same entry.
900 rather than the 700 first tried, because a truncated answer is now REFUSED rather than
shown. Measured output at low effort is 40-75 tokens for a line of dialogue, so 900 is roughly
twelve times what a subtitle needs and still leaves room for a long quest block - while
reserving 900 of Groq's 8,000 a minute instead of 4,096 is the whole point. If a model starts
logging 'answer was cut off', this is the number to raise.
llama-3.3-70b-versatile deliberately has NO reasoningEffort: it is not a reasoning model and
answers 400 '`reasoning_effort` is not supported with this model' to the parameter its two
lane-mates need. One lane, three models, two different request shapes - which is the whole
argument for these being per-model rather than per-lane.
Gemini keeps 4096 on purpose. Its free tier is metered in REQUESTS per day, its token ceilings
are in the hundreds of thousands per minute, and nothing there is bought by reserving less.
The failure mode of too small is an empty answer on every line, and that one has already cost
this project a release.
Verified-working models sit FIRST in each lane, newest do not. Every model listed here was
probed against real keys on 9 August 2026 and the order reflects what answered. A dead model
costs one fast 404 per line; an unverified model placed first risks costing the whole lane.
gemini-3.6-flash was dropped entirely: unconfirmed free-tier status, and after the timeout
lesson every extra maybe-model in the walk is worst-case latency, not safety.
Groq's order changed on 9 August: openai/gpt-oss-120b leads now. It answered in 0.53s with
clean Arabic, while llama-3.3-70b-versatile - which led this lane since 8 August because it was
the one verified survivor of that day's churn - was refusing on tokens-per-day and is deprecated
besides. It stays last rather than being dropped, because a deprecated model that still answers
is a better tail entry than nothing.
Order within the lane is preference, and it is deliberately NOT newest-first. 3.5-flash and
3.1-flash-lite are the two Google was listing on the free tier in July 2026; 3.6-flash is newer
but its free-tier status is unconfirmed, and a paid-only model at the top of this list costs
every free user a failed round trip on every single line before the fallthrough saves them.
Free-and-confirmed beats new-and-maybe. Google no longer publishes per-model free limits at
all - they are only visible in AI Studio for your own project - so this cannot be checked from
documentation and is reasoned from what the pricing page showed.
The two paid lanes' model names were checked against each provider's own model list in
August 2026. 'gpt-5.6' is deliberately the alias rather than 'gpt-5.6-sol' it points at, so a
point release does not strand this file; terra and luna are the cheaper variants behind it.
If one is ever retired the router says so by name in the Diagnostics log and falls through.
